title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Notation, from context: A_X is the Albanese variety of a smooth projective n-dimensional X, and B_X = Pic^0_X is its Picard variety. Up to isogeny conventions, A_X ≅ B_X^* (dual abelian variety).

In §2.1, which this page continues, an algebraic 1-cycle Z on X×Y defines a homomorphism u_Z : B_X → A_Y. The page treats the case where Z is the image of a morphism v = (v1, v2) : C → X×Y with C a smooth projective curve.

By the evident functoriality in X and Y, u_Z factors as
B_X --v1^*--> B_C = J_C --(autoduality of the Jacobian)--> A_C = J_C --v2_*--> A_Y.

Restated with divisorial correspondences: homomorphisms B_X → A_Y = B_Y^* correspond to divisorial correspondence classes on B_X × B_Y. The class attached to Z is the pullback, under v1^* × v2^*, of the canonical class on B_C × B_C, i.e. the theta/Poincaré class giving the principal polarization of J_C.

Specialise to X = Y and v1 = v2 = v : C → X. Then the symmetric homomorphism B_X → B_X^* = A_X is the pullback through v^* : B_X → J_C of the canonical principal polarization. The page claims four conditions are equivalent:
(i) B_X → A_X is a polarization;
(ii) it is an isogeny;
(iii) v^* : B_X → B_C has finite kernel (Grothendieck's added marginal note: 'injective mod finite groups');
(iv) v_* : A_C → A_X is surjective.

Next page: when C is a general complete intersection of very ample divisors, (iv) is the classical surjectivity J_C → Alb_X. So the correspondence B_X → A_X is an isogeny/polarization. This is then used for Prop. 2.7: the Lefschetz-type map H^1 → H^{2n-1}(n-1) is an isomorphism iff the induced map is an isogeny, and then its inverse is induced by an algebraic 1-cycle with Q-coefficients.

Purpose: the page is a step in proving the Lefschetz standard conjecture (B) in degree 1 via Picard/Albanese theory.
errors:
No mathematical error. The chain of equivalences is correct, but the justifications are left implicit:
- (iii)⇒(i): pulling back an ample class along a homomorphism with finite kernel gives an ample class.
- (ii)⇒(iii): if ker v^* has a positive-dimensional component, the pulled-back class is trivial on it, so the map is not an isogeny.
- (i)⇒(ii): holds by definition of a polarization.
- (iii)⇔(iv): v_* is the dual of v^* under A_C = B_C^* and A_X = B_X^*, and a homomorphism of abelian varieties has finite kernel iff its dual is surjective.
Identifications such as A_X ≅ B_X^* and the autoduality of J_C are used tacitly, up to sign and up to isogeny/finite groups. This is harmless for the purpose at hand.

ideas.what: Factorization of the homomorphism Pic^0_X → Alb_Y induced by a curve correspondence C → X×Y through the Jacobian of C and its autoduality.
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of Picard/Albanese under correspondences; Jacobian autoduality
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (Variétés abéliennes et courbes algébriques, 1948); Matsusaka; Lang (Abelian Varieties, 1959)
ideas.where_published: Classical; FGA treats Picard schemes but not this specific factorization

ideas.what: Homomorphisms B_X → B_Y^* identified with divisorial correspondence classes on B_X × B_Y; the induced class is the pullback of the theta class of J_C.
ideas.modern_name: Divisorial correspondences / Hom(A, B^∨) ≅ NS-type correspondence group

ideas.what: Equivalence: polarization ⇔ isogeny ⇔ v^* has finite kernel ⇔ J_C → Alb_X surjective.
ideas.modern_name: Pullback of a principal polarization along an almost-injective homomorphism is a polarization; duality of finite kernel and surjectivity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical theory of abelian varieties (Weil, Mumford)

ideas.what: Use of these facts to show that the inverse of the Lefschetz isomorphism H^1 → H^{2n-1}(n-1) is algebraic.
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz standard conjecture B(X) in degree 1
ideas.where_published: Kleiman's 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés) treats the degree ≤1 case

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but classical working-out of why a curve on X induces a polarization/isogeny Pic^0 → Alb. It is a known ingredient in the degree-1 case of the Lefschetz standard conjecture, documented by Kleiman and others. Nothing on the page appears new.
transcription_corrections: 'Il suffit donc de prouver la composée' should probably read 'Il suffit donc de prendre la composée' (or 'le composé').
'Ceci pris si X = Y' should probably read 'Ceci posé, si X = Y, v1 = v2, on voit que ...'.
'il suffit de voir[?] la classe' is probably 'il suffit de remonter la classe canonique sur B_C × B_C' (pull back along v1^*, v2^*).
The '[?]' line after 'donc' is probably 'd'où' / 'on a'.
In (iii), a letter before v^* is overwritten; v^* is the intended map.
(i) should read 'est un hom. de polarisation'.
The marginal note on (iii) is '(mod. groupes finis)', i.e. injective modulo finite groups.
